A.subject: Physics
A.text: A mass 'm' moves with a velocity 'v' and collides inelastically with another identical mass. After collision the 1st mass moves with velocity (v/√3) in a direction perpendicular to the initial direction of motion. Find the speed of the 2nd mass after collision
A.sol_text:
Answer : (1)
Solution:
Let mass A moves with velocity v and collides inelastically with mass B, which is at rest.

According to problem mass A moves in a perpendicular direction and let the mass B moves at angle θ with the horizontal with velocity v.

Initial horizontal momentum of system
(before collision) = mv
.....(i)
Final horizontal momentum of system
(after collision) = mV cos θ
.....(ii)
From the conservation of horizontal linear momentum mv = mV cos θ ⇒ v = V cos θ
....(iii)
Initial vertical momentum of system (before collision) is zero.
Final vertical momentum of system = (mv/√3) - mV sin θ

From the conservation of vertical linear momentum
(mv/√3) - mV sin θ = 0 ⇒ (v/√3) = V sin θ
....(iv)

By solving (iii) and (iv)

v² + v²/3 = V²(sin² θ + cos² θ)

⇒ (4v²/3) = V² ⇒ V = (2/√3)v

B.subject: Physics
B.text: There is a sufficiently large inclined plane making an angle α with the horizontal. A small block is given a velocity of 64 m/s perpendicular to the x-axis in the plane of the incline, the friction coefficient of which is given by μ = tan α, where α is the inclination of the plane. Find the magnitude of final velocity (in m/s) of the block.
B.sol_text:
The forces acting on the block along the plane are component of mg along x-axis and friction force along the tangential direction.
F_gr(x) = mg sin α
and f_f = μmg cos α
= (tan α)mg cos α
= mg sin α
∴ ma_t = (mg sin α) cos φ − mg sin α
= mg sin α(cos φ − 1) and ma_x = mg sin α − mg sin α cos φ
= mg sin α(1 − cos φ)
∴ a_t = −a_x or dv/dt = −dv_x/dt ∴ dv = −dv_x

∴ v = −v_x + c
∴ v = −v cos φ + c
Now, when φ = π/2, v = 64 ∴ c = 64
∴ v(1 + cos φ) = 64
∴ v = 64/(1 + cos φ)
In the course of time φ → 0 ∴ v = 64/2 = 32
B.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Number of positive integers n less than or equal to 1000 for which (sin t + i cos t)^n = sin nt + i cos nt holds true for all real t (where, i = √(-1)) is
A.sol_text:
Answer : (2)
Solution:
The question is equivalent to asking for how many positive integers n ≤ 1000 we have that (sin(π/2 - u) + i cos(π/2 - u))^n = sin n(π/2 - u) + i cos n(π/2 - u) holds for all real u.
(sin(π/2 - u) + i cos(π/2 - u))^n = (cos u + i sin u)^n = cos nu + i sin nu
Since, two complex numbers are equal if and only if both their real part and imaginary part are equal. Thus, we need to find all n such that cos nu = sin n(π/2 - u) and sin nu = cos n(π/2 - u) hold for all real u.
sin x = cos y if and only if either x + y = π/2 + 2π · k or x - y = π/2 + 2π · k for some integer k.
So, we need either nu + n(π/2 - u) = π/2 + 2π · k, in which case n = 1 + 4k, or we need -nu + n(π/2 - u) = π/2 + 2π · k, in which case n will depend on u and so the equation will not hold for all real values of u.
Checking n = 1 + 4k, in the equation for the imaginary parts, we see that it works there as well, so exactly those values of n which are of type 1 + 4k.
There are 250 of them in the given range.

A.text: Let z = a + ib be complex number with |z| = 5 such that the distance between (1 + 2i) z^3 and z^5 is maximized and let z^4 = c + di, then the value of c + d is equal to
A.sol_text:
Answer: (3)
Solution: Answer (3)
We need to maximize the value of |z^5 − (1 − 2i)z^3|.

Simplifying, we have
= |z|^3 · |z^2 − (1 − 2i)|
= 125 · |z^2 − (1 − 2i)|

Thus, we only need to maximize |z^2 − (1 − 2i)|.

For this, z^2 is in opposite direction of (1 + 2i).
The unit vector in described direction is (−1)/√5 + (−2)/√5 i.

Furthermore |z^2| = 25

∴ z^2 = √5(−5 − 10i)
∴ z^4 = −375 − 500i
∴ c + d = 125

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: How many different nine digit numbers can be formed from the number 223355888 by rearranging its digits so that the odd digits occupy even positions?
A.sol_text:
Answer: (3)
Hint:

First arrange 4 odd digits at 4 even places by (4!)/(2!|2!.) ways, then arrange the remaining digits.

Solution:
The four digits 3, 3, 5, 5 can be arranged at four even places in (4!)/(2!·2!) = 6 ways and the remaining digits viz., 2, 2, 8, 8, 8 can be arranged at the five odd places in (5!)/(2!·3!) = 10 ways. Thus, the number of possible arrangements is (6)(10) = 60.

B.text: The number of the real roots of the equation (x+1)^2 + |x-5| = 27/4 is __________.
B.sol_text:
Answer : 02.00
Solution:
If x ≥ 5
(x^2 + 2x + 1) + (x - 5) = 27/4
⇒ x^2 + 3x - 43/4 = 0
⇒ x = (-3 ± √52)/2 (No value is greater than or equal to 5)
If x < 5
x^2 + 2x + 1 - x + 5 = 27/4
⇒ x^2 + x - 3/4 = 0
⇒ x = 1/2, -3/2
So there will be two real roots.
